sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed observed-data law \(P\) in the \(\eta\)-interior binary product class.
sampling_model.treatment: Both treatment decisions are binary; the target strategy fixes \((A_0,A_1)=(1,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The six primitive coordinates \((a,q_0,e_0,e_1,p_0,p_1)\) and their complements are bounded below by \(\eta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted; the seven relevant coarsened cell probabilities are estimated by multinomial frequencies, and all empirical endpoints and branch gradients use the explicit seven-cell simplex extensions, with a deterministic fallback when an empirical cell is too small.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lemma 8 states that the sharp product-model upper bound is equivalently obtained by the normalization-constrained ratio program.
Proposition 3 bounds the sharp product-model upper endpoint by the minimum of two unconstrained optimized values.
Corollary 1 proves exactness of the two Proposition 3 components on two sensitivity-free product-model faces.
Theorem 1 gives sharp cross-sectional marginal-sensitivity bounds through one conditional quantile-balancing constraint.
The paper gives doubly sharp and doubly valid estimation for cross-sectional marginal-sensitivity endpoints.
The paper develops efficient estimators and confidence intervals for bounds under longitudinal MSM sensitivity models.
The ordinary bootstrap generally fails for nonlinear directionally differentiable maps, while derivative-aware resampling can be valid.
Gaussian-multiplier approximation is available for maxima without restrictions on cross-coordinate correlations.
The paper constructs efficient endpoint estimators and simultaneous multiplier bands under an average-case sensitivity model.

body.tldr: In the positive binary two-decision product sensitivity model of Tan (2025), exact compatibility collapses to five success probabilities and yields sharp lower and upper bounds for \(\mu_{11}\) as at most \(64\) rational branches per endpoint. Reversing the two proof chains behind Proposition 3 gives complete observable iff conditions for equality and strictness, including active ties and every sensitivity-free face. Explicit endpoint and branch maps on the seven-cell simplex then support an all-branch Gaussian-multiplier envelope with uniform asymptotic coverage for the complete sharp interval, without selecting an active branch and while allowing redundant branches and singular score covariance.

project_justification.gap: Tan's product model has exact compatibility and a generic sharp program, but its coupled ratios leave the binary endpoint implicit; Proposition 3 is only known to be conservative with selected exact faces, and sample inference is left open.
project_justification.niche: Binary intermediate covariates and outcomes retain the longitudinal compatibility problem while making every conditional ratio table exactly reducible to a success probability, which exposes both a finite frontier and the equality geometry of the relaxations.
project_justification.fill: The project proves full-data attainment for a closed-form branch atlas, completes the Proposition 3 equality-versus-strictness classification, defines matching law-indexed and seven-cell-simplex versions of every endpoint and branch, and attaches a uniformly honest multinomial confidence set for the entire identified interval.

body.related_work: Tan (2025) defines the longitudinal product ratios, proves their normalization conditions are necessary and sufficient for compatible full-data laws in Lemma 7, represents the sharp bound by a constrained program in Lemma 8, and derives two conservative Proposition 3 values with selected exact faces in Corollary 1. The present claims are an equivalence reduction of that exact program and a strict completion of that relaxation comparison, not a new sensitivity model. Dorn and Guo (2023) show that cross-sectional marginal-sensitivity extrema use normalized threshold weights; their complementary-slackness construction informs the binary threshold reduction, while Tan's sequential product normalizations create the new coupling. Dorn, Guo, and Kallus (2024) develop sharp and valid cross-sectional estimation, but do not address this longitudinal finite frontier. Bonvini et al. (2022) provide efficient estimators and confidence intervals for bounds under different longitudinal MSM sensitivity restrictions. Fang and Santos (2019) explains why an ordinary bootstrap is unreliable for a tied finite min or max and motivates derivative-aware contact sets. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) supplies Gaussian-multiplier approximation for correlated maxima; the proposed proof adds the uniform rational remainder and identified-interval coverage step. Zhang and Zhao (2026) pairs closed-form bounds with multiplier bands under an average-case cross-sectional model, providing the writing and inference exemplar rather than a theorem-level target. Rop et al. (2025) documents the limited use of sensitivity analysis in current time-varying treatment applications. Dickerman et al. (2023) supplies the applied consumer: the absolute six-year cancer risk under a repeated metformin strategy.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The endpoint reduction and strictness witness have strong algebraic and numerical presolve evidence, but the equality proof must be checked line by line against the final Proposition 3 formulas. The coverage theorem still requires a written uniform Gaussian-quantile argument using the explicit seven-cell simplex branches and at least one uniformly nondegenerate branch score while allowing other branch coordinates to have zero variance. No claim concerns contrasts between treatment strategies, sign breakdown, continuous outcomes, more than two decisions, efficiency, or shortest confidence sets.
body.honest_scope: The finite endpoint representation, full-data attainment, equality frontier, strict witness, exact agreement of the law-indexed and seven-cell-simplex maps, remainder lemma, and uniform coverage theorem are all posed as results to prove. The contact-set-adaptive improvement is deliberately isolated as the open-ended question. At \(G=B=C=1\), the proposal must reduce to the standard g-formula. The empirical consumer is the absolute sustained-strategy risk only.
